messages:
alex: quick heads up — ran a perfetto capture for a 1000qps e2e run and see a repeating pattern where kernel selection flips between conv-deconv variants mid-request, causing ~40ms tail spikes

maria: ugh that sounds like the hysteresis we saw before. do you have the perfetto slice? link?

alex: attached the trace to the perfetto viewer, but here's the quick CLI I used to capture:
```
nsys profile -o perf_run1 --trace=cuda,nvtx python -m app.load_test --qps 1000 --duration 5m
perfetto --txt -o trace.pb
```

derek: can you paste the waterfall around one of the spikes? want to see client->gateway->runtime spans and the kernel timelines aligned

alex: pasted a 12s waterfall excerpt below. you can see gateway span ends, runtime span starts, then two kernel switches: conv_small -> deconv_tiled -> conv_small. the KV cache lookup also shows a miss sequence before the first swap.

ingrid: small note — if KV miss triggers a longer dispatch path it can change the batch composition. that could cause the runtime to pick the deconv variant because estimated sequence length changed

maria: yeah, the selector uses batch median sequence length and micro-batching heuristics. a KV miss that invalidates prefix cache will push sequences to longer runtime budget, flipping kernel scoring.

alex: exact timeline snippet (nsys timeline labels):
```
[0.000s] gateway_end (nvtx)
[0.003s] runtime_recv
[0.006s] KVCache: lookup miss -> fetch remote
[0.012s] kernel_launch: conv_small
[0.025s] kernel_launch: deconv_tiled
[0.038s] kernel_launch: conv_small
[0.080s] runtime_send
```

derek: interesting that deconv_tiled is inserted in the middle. maybe the kernel scoring function recomputed after the fetch completes and saw a different token distribution

ingrid: can we correlate with batch boundaries? if the gateway batches requests with slight jitter, the fetch latency could shift one request into next micro-batch. that would change the chosen kernel because we use per-batch heuristics.

maria: next steps I propose: 1) reproduce with KV cache forced-miss and forced-hit traces, 2) run nsys with kernel stats to check occupancy and heuristics logs, 3) add a short debounce window in kernel selector to avoid flip-flops.

alex: I ran a quick A/B: forced-hit vs forced-miss. result: forced-hit tail p99 ~ 78ms, forced-miss p99 ~ 122ms, and we see 35-45ms micro-spikes matching the deconv insertion.

derek: can you share the exact nsys command you used? need the api timing counters.

alex: here it is, verbatim:
```
nsys profile --stats=true -o nsys_kernels --trace=cuda,osrt,api python -m app.load_test --qps 1000 --duration 2m
```

maria: when you open the nsys result, look at kernel 3 and kernel 7 in the table. kernel 7 is the deconv tiled variant showing much higher sm_efficiency but also higher latency for short sequences. kernel 3 is conv_small optimized for short tokens. the selector mispredicted because it uses average token length, not tail percentiles.

ingrid: we should tweak the scoring to prefer lower-latency kernel for 90th pct length rather than mean. that reduces regrets when KV miss inflates a few sequences.

perf-bot: incident-detection: recurring kernel flip pattern observed in traces 5x across last 3 captures; related tag: kernel-selection-oscillation

maria: thanks perf-bot. also noticed a batching heuristic edge: our micro-batch flush timeout is 6ms, but the KV remote fetch can add 5-10ms jitter; moving flush timeout to 3ms reduced flips in my quick run but slightly increased average token cost. tradeoff to consider.

derek: what about adding a transient pin: if a batch has already started executing conv_small, schedule the next micro-batch to prefer conv_small for up to 2 subsequent batches unless strong evidence to switch. simplest debounce.

alex: implemented a temporary selector debounce on my local branch: if kernel changed, require 2 consecutive scoring votes to switch. re-run results: p99 dropped to 95ms (from 122ms) on forced-miss, but average latency went up 6ms overall.

maria: promising. could we make debounce adaptive: small batches get shorter debounce, large batches longer? also add metric to console showing flip-rate per minute.

ingrid: yes and expose an opt-in config per-customer under Dedicated where they can pick conservative selector for SLO-sensitive workloads.

derek: one more thing — add nvtx markers around KV cache lookup and batch commit so traces can be filtered by span quickly. also record selector inputs into NVTX so perf analysis can replay decisions.

alex: added NVTX hooks locally and uploaded a new perfetto with the richer annotations. uploading link to the viewer now.

maria: can someone open a small RFC? include: cause analysis, debounce experiment data, config knobs, and rollout plan (canary on dedicated pools). I can draft the rollout doc.

alex: will paste the quick experiment numbers into RFC draft. thanks all, good triage. :thumbsup:
